classification.difficultyReason: Uses tangent-radius perpendicularity, similar right triangles and externally tangent radii to derive an inverse sine ratio.

content.prompt: The circles shown below are tangent, and $DE$ is tangent to both circles. The line segment $AC$ passes through the centres of both circles. Find $\theta$, correct to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: Two externally tangent circles with collinear centres B and C and external point A. Their common upper tangent touches at D and E. Both tangent-radius right angles, radii 1 and 2, all five point labels and the angle at A are preserved. No shading.
spec.mathematics: BD=1, CE=2, BC=3; BD and CE are perpendicular to AE. Coordinates derive from sin(theta)=1/3 and produce exact tangencies.
spec.answerVisibility: Question diagram contains only source givens; no derived lengths or angle value are displayed.

inlines.text: Similar right triangles give AC = 2AB; the tangent circles give BC = 3, so AB = 3.

answer.worked:
A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at its point of contact. Triangles $ABD$ and $ACE$ are therefore similar: both are right-angled and share the angle at $A$.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{AC}{AB}&=\frac{CE}{BD}\\\frac{AC}{AB}&=2\\AC&=2AB\end{align*}$$
The circles touch externally, so $BC=1+2=3$ and $AC=AB+3$.
$$\begin{align*}2AB&=AB+3\\AB&=3\\\sin\theta&=\frac{BD}{AB}\\\sin\theta&=\frac{1}{3}\\\theta&=\sin^{-1}\!\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)\\\theta&\approx19.47^\circ\end{align*}$$
